Task: kanban-columns-drag-reorder

## WHAT & WHY

In any pipeline's Kanban view (`src/app/features/board.jsx`) the user should be
able to rearrange the columns by grabbing a column's header (the title bar,
`kcol-h`) and dragging it to the position they want. Today the columns are a
fixed derivation — the union of every stage used by the pipeline's tasks plus a
terminal "Delivered" column — with no way to reorder them. Dragging the title
and dropping it in the right place lets the user arrange the board to match how
they actually work, in every pipeline.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- Column headers are draggable; a drag gives visual feedback (grabbed style)
  and a drop indicator showing where the column will land.
- Dropping over a valid slot moves that column (with its cards) to that
  position; cancelling (Escape) or dropping outside leaves the order unchanged.
- The reordered order PERSISTS per pipeline and survives reload/reopen — stored
  on the pipeline's own metadata (e.g. a `kanbanOrder` field in
  `.bridza/pipelines/<pipeline>/.metadata/metadata.json`), committed like
  `savePipeline`/`archivePipeline` in `server/bridza-store.js`, and exposed
  through a new bridge endpoint in `server/bridge.js`. NOT global/localStorage —
  each pipeline keeps its own order.
- Other pipelines keep their own stored order; a pipeline with no stored order
  falls back to today's derived ordering.
- Uses existing CSS tokens in `bridza.css`; no new drag-and-drop library unless
  native HTML5 drag & drop proves insufficient (flag it in review.md if added).
- Unit tests cover the reorder and per-pipeline persistence logic; `pnpm test`
  passes, and `pnpm lint` + `pnpm build` are clean.

NOTE: sibling sub-task `kanban-archive-issue-cards` also edits
`src/app/features/board.jsx` on a separate branch — keep changes localised to
the column-header/ordering path so the two merge cleanly.

$ claude -p "Task: kanban-columns-drag-reorder" --permission-mode acceptEdits --model opus --append-system-prompt "You are a senior engineer. Write spec.md + acceptance.md from the task intent only. The smallest spec that answers what, why, and how we'll know it works — n…"
I've written `spec.md` and `acceptance.md` for dragging Kanban columns into a new order that's saved per pipeline. They're in `.bridza/pipelines/engineering/kanban-columns-drag-reorder/spec/outputs/`. I haven't committed anything.

**The plan in the spec:**
- **Ordering:** two small helper functions exported from `board.jsx`, both unit-tested:
  - `applyKanbanOrder(derived, stored)` puts the saved columns first, in saved order, then adds any new columns in today's order and ignores saved ids that no longer exist.
  - `moveColumn(order, fromId, toIndex)` returns the new order after one drag.
- **Dragging:** column headers use the browser's built-in drag and drop, with no new library. The dragged header gets a "grabbed" style and a marker shows where it will land. Escape or dropping outside the board leaves the order as it was. The new order shows immediately and is then saved; if saving fails, the board goes back to the old order and shows the error.
- **Saving:**
  - A new `saveKanbanOrder` in `server/bridza-store.js`, built the same way as `archivePipeline`, writes `kanbanOrder` into that pipeline's `metadata.json` and commits it.
  - `readProject` builds each pipeline object by hand, so it has to be changed to include `kanbanOrder`. Without that the saved order would never reach the board.
  - A new endpoint, `POST /api/bridza/pipeline/kanban-order`, and a matching `saveKanbanOrder` in `src/app/api/client.js`.
- **Merging with the sibling task:** card markup and card handlers stay untouched, so this branch should merge cleanly with `kanban-archive-issue-cards`, which edits the cards in `board.jsx`.

**Decisions to confirm:**
- **Delivered can be dragged too.** It's treated like any other column, which keeps the logic simpler.
- **Out of scope:** changing the order of stages within a flow, moving cards between columns, reordering by keyboard only, and a "reset order" button.

The `spec.md` and `acceptance.md` at the repo root are from the earlier welcome-dialog task, and I left them alone.

The design, Figma and planning connectors (Figma, Asana, Atlassian, Linear, Notion, Slack, Intercom, Google Calendar) aren't authorized; they weren't needed here. To use them later, connect the claude.ai ones in your claude.ai connector settings and the others with `/mcp` in an interactive session.

I've built column-header drag-to-reorder for the Kanban, with the order saved per pipeline. **I haven't run any checks:** `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build`, and even `npx vitest` all needed approval that this session couldn't give. The tests are written but have never been run, and nothing is committed yet.

**What's in place:**
- **Dragging** (`src/app/features/board.jsx`): every column header, Delivered included, can be dragged using the browser's built-in drag and drop, with no new library. While dragging, the header is dimmed and a blue bar shows where the column will land. Pressing Escape or dropping outside a column changes nothing and saves nothing.
- **Order logic** (`src/app/features/board.jsx`): two small helpers, `applyKanbanOrder` and `moveColumn`. A pipeline with no saved order shows today's order. If the saved order is out of date, stages that no longer exist are ignored and new stages are added after the saved ones.
- **Saving:** the new order shows straight away, then goes to a new `saveKanbanOrder` in `server/bridza-store.js`. It writes `kanbanOrder` into that pipeline's `metadata.json` and commits only that file. It rejects an unknown pipeline or an order that isn't a list of strings. If the save fails, the board goes back to the previous order and shows the error.
- **Connections:** a new endpoint `POST /api/bridza/pipeline/kanban-order` in `server/bridge.js`, and a matching call in `src/app/api/client.js`. `readProject` now returns `kanbanOrder` for each pipeline, empty if none is saved. Editing a pipeline's stage flow keeps its saved order, because `savePipeline` keeps fields it doesn't change.
- **Styles** (`src/app/bridza.css`): four rules using the existing `--accent` and `--bg-3` colours.
- **Tests:** a new `src/app/__tests__/kanban-order.test.js` covers the order logic. A new case in `bridza-store.test.js` covers saving, the commit, reading the order back, each pipeline keeping its own order, and the rejected inputs.

The card markup and card handlers in `board.jsx` are unchanged, so it should merge cleanly with `kanban-archive-issue-cards`.
